brief.outcome: Grow the cooking channel for busy parents from 2,050 subscribers toward 10,000 within a year, on one self-filmed video a week and without clickbait.

ambition.goal_beyond: The channel grows reliably on one video a week, so growth comes from a method that works and not from a lucky hit.
rungs: Write better titles and thumbnails for the next videos.

Find from all 85 videos what really holds growth back (packaging, the first 30 seconds, topic, length or how viewers are asked to subscribe), fix the biggest cause first, and say honestly how far 10,000 is from what the data supports.
Keep it true: a short weekly check of the same measures that feeds the next video, so the method keeps improving.
ambition.judge: YouTube Studio's own analytics export per video (impressions, click-through rate, average percentage viewed, subscribers gained) and the results of YouTube's title and thumbnail tests, compared across the same number of videos before and after.

brief.deliverable: A diagnosis from all 85 videos, a chosen plan, an eight-video pack (titles, thumbnails, hooks and outlines) in the owner's style, tests and uploads run with the owner's approval, and a weekly readout against the 10,000 goal.

Rules saved for the next quarter

guardrails: No clickbait or misleading thumbnails or titles
Average percentage viewed does not fall when click-through rises (a click gain that costs retention does not count)
The channel stays at one self-filmed video a week; hours per video do not rise
No bought subscribers, no sub-for-sub swaps
Nothing is changed on the channel without the owner's yes

answers.question: What is the channel and how big?
answers.answer: Cooking channel for busy parents, 85 videos over two years, 2,050 subscribers.

answers.question: What do the numbers look like?
answers.answer: Average video gets 900 views; click-through rate about 3.1% and average view duration 2:40 on 12-minute videos (YouTube Studio, reported).

answers.question: How is it made?
answers.answer: I film one video a week myself.

answers.question: Target, access and rules?
answers.answer: 10,000 subscribers within a year. YouTube Studio access through the browser. I will not do clickbait or misleading thumbnails.

answers.question: Data home and who decides?
answers.answer: Keep notes in this project. I decide.

answers.question: My guess for what should happen after this (ambition)
answers.answer: Accepted as the working guess: you want a method that grows the channel steadily on one video a week, so we find the cause first and set the target against what the data supports.

research.approach: Practitioners start from the per-video analytics table, not channel averages, and read three things together: how often the video is shown and clicked (impressions and click-through), how long people stay (retention, especially the first 30 seconds) and whether viewers subscribe. YouTube's own guidance says half of channels sit between 2% and 10% click-through, so 3.1% is typical, while 2:40 on a 12-minute video is about 22% viewed, which points at the opening and the video's shape. They compare like with like (similar length and topic, similar traffic source), judge by the median video and not by one hit, and avoid pushing click-through by misleading packaging, because YouTube treats that as a policy breach and a high click rate with low viewing hurts. They then change one thing at a time, using YouTube's own title and thumbnail test (which picks a winner by watch time share) and a before-and-after comparison across several videos, read at a set age such as 28 days. The target is checked against what each upload currently earns in subscribers.

sources.title: Impressions click-through rate (YouTube Help)
sources.note: Page shows no publication date; accessed 2026-11-03. Platform documentation: half of channels and videos have a click-through between 2% and 10%; compare over time and by traffic source; a high click rate with low view duration can indicate clickbait.

sources.title: Audience retention (YouTube Help)
sources.note: Page shows no publication date; accessed 2026-11-03. Platform documentation: intro retention is the share still watching after 30 seconds; read flat lines, dips and spikes; compare with your own similar-length videos; segment new versus returning and subscribers versus not.

sources.title: A/B test titles and thumbnails (YouTube Help)
sources.note: Page shows no publication date; accessed 2026-11-03. Platform documentation: test up to three titles or thumbnails on desktop in Studio; winner is chosen by watch time share, not click-through; tests finish within two weeks; low-impression videos are often inconclusive.

sources.title: Spam, deceptive practices and scams policy (YouTube Help)
sources.note: Page shows no publication date; accessed 2026-11-03. Platform policy: maliciously misleading titles, thumbnails, descriptions or imagery are prohibited.

sources.title: Mistakes small YouTube channels make (vidIQ)
sources.note: Practitioner vendor, published 2024-02-01 and reviewed 2026-08-14: spend more time on titles and thumbnails, work on the first 30 seconds, avoid chasing the wrong metrics. Qualitative, with no data.

steps.name: Export the per-video table and traffic sources for all 85 videos
steps.why: Averages hide which videos, topics and sources move the channel; the raw table shows them.

steps.name: Check the numbers and set the comparison groups
steps.why: Click-through counts only some impressions, new videos need time, and a few hits skew the average.

steps.name: Read click-through, first 30 seconds, retention shape, topic and subscribe rate together
steps.why: Each cause needs a different fix and several can act at once.

steps.name: Check the 10,000 target against subscribers gained per upload
steps.why: A target is only useful if it is set beside what each video earns today.

steps.name: Write packaging, hooks and outlines for the next videos within the policy
steps.why: Packaging and the opening are the cheapest levers for a solo channel, and misleading packaging breaks policy.

steps.name: Test one change at a time with YouTube's own tests and a before-and-after across videos
steps.why: A single test on a low-impression video is often inconclusive; comparing several videos and reading at a set age is steadier.

steps.name: Read weekly at a fixed video age and keep what works
steps.why: A short weekly look on the same measures shows what to repeat, improve or stop.

pitfalls.text: Raising click-through with misleading packaging, which can lower viewing time and break YouTube's policy.
Judging a thumbnail test with too few impressions, or changing a title or thumbnail mid-test.
Reading the channel average, so one or two hits hide a weak median video.
Chasing the wrong metric, such as raw click-through, instead of watch time and subscribers per view.

plan.name: Find what holds the channel back and fix it video by video

capabilities.name: Read YouTube Studio analytics (browser)
capabilities.why: Export the per-video table, traffic sources and retention curves.

capabilities.name: Change titles and thumbnails, start tests and schedule uploads (YouTube Studio)
capabilities.why: Apply the chosen packaging and uploads; each action waits for the owner's yes.

data.name: Per-video analytics for all 85 videos
data.why: The raw material: every video's reach, clicks, viewing and subscribers.

routes.how: YouTube Studio, Analytics, Advanced mode, Content: set the lifetime range, show the table with these columns, and Export.
If Advanced mode is unavailable, screenshots of the content table sorted by views, in pages.

data.alternative: Without it, only channel averages exist; causes by video, topic and length stay unknown.

data.name: Traffic sources and audience
data.why: Shows whether views come from search, browse or suggested, and how many viewers are new or returning.

stages.name: Confirm the brief
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured goal, limits and what is unknown. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Export the channel's raw numbers
stages.goal: Export the per-video table for all 85 videos, the traffic-source and audience data, and retention curves for a sample of 15 videos into the project.

checks.name: The file has all 85 videos, or lists each missing one
Total views and total subscribers gained in the file match Studio's channel totals for the same dates within 1%
Each video is tagged with a topic group and a length band

stages.name: Check the numbers and set the comparison groups
stages.goal: Check that the reported 3.1%, 2:40 and 900 views reproduce from the table, flag videos too new or too small to judge, and set groups to compare by length, topic and traffic source. Use the median, not the average.

checks.name: The reported averages are reproduced from the table within 5%, or the gap is explained
Videos under 28 days old or with under 100 views are excluded from comparisons and listed
Median and average views are both shown and the share of views from the top 5 videos is stated
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the diagnosis

stages.name: Find what holds growth back
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses against the table, traffic sources and retention curves, and check how far 10,000 is from what each upload earns in subscribers. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN with the numbers behind it
A group is called better only with at least 8 videos in it, otherwise low-confidence
Each main finding names a competing explanation
States subscribers per upload now and the amount per upload that 10,000 in a year needs

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked change cards (opening, packaging, topic or series, length, subscribe ask), each with the finding behind it, expected effect, effort for one video a week, confidence, risk and how it will be measured.

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card states added hours per video, and none raises hours per video
The set says what growth the supported changes can reasonably give against 10,000, with the uncertainty

stages.name: Owner chooses the plan
stages.goal: The owner picks the cards, the success rule per change and the target they will hold themselves to. Ask why when the top card is passed over.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are recorded with reasons
Each change has a keep, adjust or stop rule with numbers written before it is tried

stages.name: Write the next eight videos' packaging and hooks
stages.goal: For the next eight weekly videos, write title and thumbnail options (one tested pair each), the first-30-seconds hook and an outline in the owner's style, plus the subscribe ask the plan calls for. Check each against YouTube's misleading-metadata rule and the owner's no-clickbait rule.

checks.name: Each title and thumbnail promises only what the video shows, and each pair differs in one thing
Each hook is scored and states the payoff in the first 30 seconds
No video needs more filming or editing hours than the owner's current weekly video
Every element traces to a chosen card

stages.name: Apply the tests and upload
stages.goal: Register each change with its baseline and rule, then start title and thumbnail tests on old and new videos and schedule the weekly uploads in Studio, one approved action at a time. Change one thing per video group.

checks.name: Each change and its baseline are in experiments.jsonl before it goes live
Each title, thumbnail and test setting is read back from Studio and matches the approved pack
No title or thumbnail is changed during a running test

stages.name: Weekly readout at a fixed video age
stages.goal: Each week read the newest videos at 28 days and the tests' results from Studio's own data, compared with the previous eight videos on click-through, average percentage viewed, subscribers per 1,000 views and the gap to 10,000.

checks.name: Videos are compared at the same age and, where possible, the same topic group and length band
Average percentage viewed on new videos is not more than 10% below the previous eight; a click-through gain that breaks this is not counted
A change is judged only with at least 8 videos in each group, or a test labelled Winner by Studio; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE

stages.name: Keep what worked and plan the next quarter
stages.goal: Close each experiment, save rules with their scope, and plan the next quarter's changes and a revised target against the data.

checks.name: Every experiment is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each saved rule says whether it applies to one video type, this channel or any channel
The 10,000 target is restated with the number of subscribers per upload the data supports

hypotheses.statement: Viewers leave in the opening, so most videos end with about a fifth of the video watched.
hypotheses.test: Intro retention at 30 seconds and the shape of the curve for the 5 best, 5 median and 5 weakest recent videos; average percentage viewed (2:40 of 12:00 is about 22%) across all videos.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Intro retention on the weakest 5 is at least 15 points below the best 5 and the steepest drop is inside the first 30 seconds on at least 3 of the weakest 5.
hypotheses.refute_if: The steepest drop is later in the video, or intro retention is within 5 points across best and weakest.

hypotheses.statement: Titles and thumbnails limit views because too few viewers click.
hypotheses.test: Views against click-through across the 85 videos; compare videos by click-through quartile with impressions held similar.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Videos in the top quarter for click-through have at least 1.5 times the median views, and the bottom quarter sit below 2.5% click-through.
hypotheses.refute_if: Click-through shows no link to views, or the bottom quarter is still within the 2% to 10% typical band with similar views.

hypotheses.statement: Few people are shown the videos, because impressions are low or flat, not because clicks are weak.
hypotheses.test: Impressions per video and traffic-source mix for the last 20 videos compared with the first 20 comparable ones; share of views from search, browse and suggested.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Median impressions on the last 20 videos are not higher than on the first 20, while click-through stays inside 2% to 10%.
hypotheses.refute_if: Impressions are rising steadily and click-through is falling.

hypotheses.statement: A few topic groups bring most new viewers, and the channel does not make enough of them.
hypotheses.test: Tag the 85 videos by topic group; views from non-subscribers and subscribers gained per group, against share of uploads.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Three topic groups give at least half of non-subscriber views from under 30% of the uploads.
hypotheses.refute_if: Non-subscriber views are spread evenly across groups.

hypotheses.statement: Twelve minutes is too long for these recipes, so the share of the video watched is low.
hypotheses.test: Average percentage viewed by length band, with at least 8 videos per band.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Videos under 8 minutes show an average percentage viewed at least 10 points above videos over 10 minutes.
hypotheses.refute_if: Average percentage viewed is within 5 points across length bands.

hypotheses.statement: Viewers watch but do not subscribe, because there is no clear reason or ask.
hypotheses.test: Subscribers gained per 1,000 views per video, and whether the video has a spoken ask or series framing.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Videos with a spoken ask or series framing gain at least double the subscribers per 1,000 views of those without, across 8 or more videos each.
hypotheses.refute_if: Subscribers per 1,000 views are the same with and without an ask.

hypotheses.statement: 10,000 in a year needs far more subscribers per upload than the channel earns now.
hypotheses.test: Subscribers gained over the last 20 videos divided by 20, against the roughly 7,950 new subscribers a year needed, which is about 150 per weekly upload.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Subscribers per upload over the last 20 videos are under a quarter of the amount needed per upload.
hypotheses.refute_if: Subscribers per upload are already above half of the amount needed.

measurement.window: Each video read at 28 days, weekly for eight videos per change, then monthly; title and thumbnail tests run up to two weeks as Studio allows.
measurement.min_volume: At least 8 videos in each comparison group, or a Studio test result of Winner; below that the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.
measurement.stop_rule: Revert a change if average percentage viewed falls more than 10% below the previous eight videos for two videos in a row, or if the packaging is judged misleading; otherwise run the full window.
